explanation: Broad query-gated previous-token head: the current word's query controls attention back to the previous token (gradable adjectives after how/what attend it at ~0.9 while pronouns and nouns mostly self-attend), so ordinary multi-word prose is active-weak (peaks 0.25-0.4x scale) and strong peaks (>=0.4x) occur only on the second word of a tight left-licensing pair: a gradable adjective/adverb after how/what (how good/much/well/often), a bare verb after infinitival to or a preverbal quantifier (to compensate, Both were), a gerund after When (When running), a plural noun after a numeral/quantifier (two sides, both directions, either side), or a content noun after what (what values/precautions). Non-licensing continuations are locally weak (how it/the, the + noun, verb + how), and only single-word/interjection texts, bare numeric strings, and short probes with no licensing pair stay fully below the line.
